resident evil 3 remake isn t scary.. it s scripted. nemesis, once the unstoppable nightmare of the original, is now reduced to predictable cutscenes and over-the-top boss fights. no tension, no dread, just spectacle. whole sections of the original game are gone no clock tower, no park, no branching paths, no meaningful exploration. the city feels tiny, the puzzles are brain-dead simple, and the campaign is over before you know it. what s left is a short, linear action game that trades atmosphere and replay value for flashy set pieces. it s not the worst game out there, but if you came for survival horror, you ll leave disappointed. remake nemesis is just a shell of a popular horror icon. if you get it for free or in a bundle, sure, add it to your library.. it s a decent weekend distraction. but as a full-price purchase? not recommended.

the game itself is fun, a lot of unique characters and maps, but what makes me unable to recommend this game to anyone is matchmaking. marvel rivals uses engagement-optimized matchmaking eomm, which means the game doesn't prioritize giving you fair matches but matches that are most likely to keep you playing. the result of that are massive winstreaks and massive losestreaks. every game is a steamroll for one side and your actions feel useless. you could be the best player on the game but if you are on a lose streak it will not matter how good you are. the opposite is also true, you could run off the map and contribute nothing to your team, but if you are on a win streak you are gonna win. as long as marvel rivals keeps this matchmaking system in place i can not recommend this game to anyone. the first few matches are fun but when you realize how it works it just makes you not want to turn the game on which you can see if you look at steam charts.

cleaned_text: sins of a solar empire ii is the kind of game that lulls you into thinking you re just managing a calm little space empire right up until three different factions declare war on you and your peaceful trading routes become galactic shooting galleries. it s a real-time strategy game with the scale of a 4x colonising planets, building fleets, researching tech, and inevitably realising you ve neglected defences on that one critical system. combat is massive and cinematic, but you ll also spend half your time zoomed out to the point where your mighty armada looks like glitter in a void. diplomacy exists, but usually boils down to bribing someone not to annihilate you for ten minutes. it s complex, it s grand, and it s just stressful enough to make you feel like the un secretary-general if the un had battleships and orbital nukes. great for anyone who s ever wanted to run a space empire and accidentally start a galaxy-wide apocalypse.

world of tanks is a solid game to drop into when you have some time to kill, but it is not a must-play masterpiece. the tank combat is genuinely engaging it has enough tactical depth with its armor angling and spotting mechanics to make you feel smart when you pull off a good play, and the enormous variety of historical tanks means there is always something new to unlock. the thrill of grinding up a tech tree and finally earning that coveted tier x is a great feeling. however, be warned that the experience is highly inconsistent. it is often frustrating due to seemingly random shot dispersion and shell non-penetrations, and the lengthy grind in the later tiers is clearly structured to encourage you to spend real money. if you can approach it casually, laugh off the losses, and just enjoy piloting those awesome tanks, you'll have fun. but if you are looking for the most competitive or best-balanced experience on steam, this isn't it.

the outlast trials is a co-op survival horror where you are thrown into gloomy cold war laboratories, forced to undergo brutal tests for freedom. unlike previous parts, here you can and should! play with friends the single player mode is more difficult, and the enemies are sometimes annoying - their attacks are sometimes easy to avoid, sometimes impossible to predict. the atmosphere is oppressive an alarming soundtrack, flickering light and bloody locations plunge you into paranoia. survival depends on stealth and luck - one mistake at the end of the mission crosses out 40 minutes of progress. the graphics are not revolutionary, but the detail pleases. ideal for fans of the series and lovers of co-op, but it quickly becomes boring. it is worth playing for the adrenaline and an evening with friends, but it is unlikely to hook you for more than 100 hours.
